mechanism: header-index-file-path and header-index-delta-path (src/storage/chain.lisp:929-931,947-951) derive from chain-state-base-path ONLY -- the storage-suffix that separates chainstate_snapshot/ from chainstate/ (chain.lisp:588-600) is not applied to them -- so every chainstate writes the SAME headerindex.dat and headerindex.delta. The two slots that bind a delta log to the snapshot it extends, chain-state-header-index-snapshot-crc and -delta-entries (chain.lisp:46-52), are per chain-state STRUCT and %make-snapshot-chainstate (src/node/assumeutxo.lisp:39-53) copies neither: it shares :block-index with the primary and leaves the crc NIL. save-header-index (chain.lisp:1121-1148) treats a NIL crc as 'no usable snapshot' and takes the %write-header-index-snapshot branch, which rewrites the whole shared index, DELETES the delta and adopts the new file's CRC for THAT chainstate only (chain.lisp:1046-1056); the other chainstate's crc now names a snapshot that no longer exists and nothing ever refreshes it, because a non-NIL crc plus an existing file always routes to the append branch. %append-header-index-delta stamps the crc of whichever chainstate CREATES the log into its 12-byte header (chain.lisp:1079-1090) and never re-checks it on later appends, so when the stale chainstate opens the log every frame in it -- including frames appended by the healthy chainstate -- is bound to a dead snapshot, and %replay-header-index-delta discards the whole file at the next start (chain.lisp:1197-1204). Both chainstates are flushed every cycle: maybe-periodic-flush calls %flush-chainstate on the triggering chainstate and then on every other (src/node/flush.lisp:386-389), and %flush-chainstate Phase 1 calls save-header-index unconditionally (flush.lisp:250-251). Core cannot reach this: the block index and everything that persists it live in BlockManager outside any chainstate (refs/bitcoin/src/node/blockstorage.cpp:407-421,510-527), so adding a snapshot chainstate adds no second copy of the persistence state.
consequence: On a node that has run loadtxoutset (the only way to get a second chainstate: %make-snapshot-chainstate is reached from create-snapshot-chainstate via the RPC and from load-snapshot-chainstate's startup re-detection, src/node/assumeutxo.lisp:62,149 -- it is NOT reachable at default settings), every block-index mutable field changed since the last FULL snapshot is silently dropped at the next unclean stop: statuses (:valid / :invalid), tx-count, and file / data-pos / undo-pos. Executed, the stale binding never heals while the node runs -- six flush cycles with cs1 at crc 9cc337f2 while the on-disk snapshot was bd04887d -- and the delta log created by the stale chainstate carried 9cc337f2 in its header, so the reload restored tx-counts (1 0 0 0 0 0) where (1 2 3 4 5 6) had been persisted. The sharpest edge is an operator invalidateblock silently reverting to the pre-mark status; recently connected blocks come back header-only and are re-downloaded; a lost undo-pos defeats %save-undo-flat's write-once guard so the next disconnect appends a duplicate undo record; a lost data-pos loses the body location. Nothing is logged. Two things bound it below S1: a CLEAN shutdown heals it (%shutdown-flush-chainstates force-fulls every chainstate, src/node/shutdown.lisp:368, and the executed control kept an :INVALID mark across that path), and a reverted :invalid does not put a bad block on the chain -- %reorg-connect re-validates every fork block body it connects (src/validation/block.lisp:3475-3495), so the block is re-rejected rather than served as valid. The coins DB and chainstate.dat are untouched.
evidence: Probes under build/ga11v/ (git-ignored) loaded into BITCOIN-LISP.TESTS and run through scripts/dev.sh eval on the project container in worktree bl-ga11v-storage-s2. (1) ga11v-p1, the finder's shape reproduced independently: cs1 wrote the full snapshot (crc c1be5ead); a cs2 built exactly as %make-snapshot-chainstate builds it (same base-path, :block-index shared, :storage-suffix "_snapshot") reported (:CS2-CRC-AT-BIRTH NIL) with (:SAME-INDEX-P T) and (:SAME-HIDX-PATH T :SAME-DELTA-PATH T); after cs1 appended a delta, cs2's save wrote a full snapshot, deleted the delta and took 5f4f0b18 while cs1 kept c1be5ead (:CRCS-AGREE NIL); an :invalid mark then persisted through cs1 read back (:E3-STATUS :VALID :EXPECTED-E3 :INVALID) with (:DELTA-FILE-STILL-THERE NIL) -- the loader deleted the log. (2) ga11v-p1b, the two counter-probes: six consecutive flush cycles left (:CS1 "9cc337f2" :CS2 "bd04887d") unchanged, the log header read (:LOG-HEADER-CRC "9cc337f2" :ON-DISK-SNAPSHOT-CRC "bd04887d"), the reload gave (:TX-COUNTS-AFTER-RELOAD (1 0 0 0 0 0) :EXPECTED (1 2 3 4 5 6)), and the clean-shutdown control (save-header-index :force-full t on each, then reload) gave (:CLEAN-SHUTDOWN-STATUS :INVALID :EXPECTED :INVALID). Ours: src/storage/chain.lisp:46-52,588-600,929-931,947-951,1025-1056,1070-1113,1121-1148,1163-1250,1253-1289; src/node/assumeutxo.lisp:39-53,62,149; src/node/flush.lisp:209-251,386-389; src/node/shutdown.lisp:352-368. Core at d3056bc: refs/bitcoin/src/node/blockstorage.cpp:407-421,510-527.
fix_shape: Do not implement here. Core's shape is that there is exactly one persistence state for one block index, so the fix is to move the binding off the chain-state struct rather than to copy it. Smallest Core-faithful form: keep header-index-snapshot-crc and header-index-delta-entries with the THING they describe -- the shared headerindex.dat -- as a per-base-path record (a small struct on the block index, or a datadir-keyed singleton the way bl.store already keys the block store), so save-header-index and %replay-header-index-delta read one crc no matter which chainstate is flushing, and %make-snapshot-chainstate has nothing left to forget. Whatever the carrier, %append-header-index-delta must also verify the crc it reads back from an EXISTING log's header against its own before appending (today it only writes the header when the log is fresh), so a mismatched pair fails over to a full snapshot instead of silently poisoning frames a healthy writer contributed. A test should pin it end to end: two chain-states on one base-path with a shared block index, alternating saves, an :invalid mark persisted through the non-creating one, and a reload asserting the mark survived -- with the positive control that the same test goes red when the crc slots are made per-struct again.
